answer: A new agent cannot mint standing on its own; it must be grafted onto an established one's bonded identity, the way a cutting is spliced onto a living vine, so every duplicate inherits its sponsor's liability. Fabricating a thousand puppets costs a thousand bond postings, and if any single one misbehaves mid-voyage, the penalty climbs the graft back to the sponsor and collapses that whole knoll of accounts at once.
